A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LD3 research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V2 reports original image-generation experiments, component ablations, solver-transfer tests, training analyses, and prompt-variation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original LD3 experiments and adds point-cloud generation, molecular docking, and an NCSN++ experiment for comparison with consistency distillation.

M1.justification: The central objectives, time parameterization, and time decoupling remain unchanged. V3 introduces a limited adaptation converting DiffDock's reverse-SDE sampler to an ODE. Algorithm 1 also changes the base point of the printed projection update from x'_T to x_T, consistent with the projection center already described in v2's prose.

E1.justification: V2's actual evaluations concern image generation. V3 Appendix B adds ShapeNet airplane point-cloud generation and protein–ligand docking evaluated against PDB reference structures, substantially extending the represented domains and task requirements. Existing image-task coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V3 adds teacher reference comparisons to the existing image benchmarks in Tables 2 and 4 and includes DMN and GITS in expanded qualitative comparisons previously showing LD3 against a single heuristic. The principal discretization and distillation comparator families remain unchanged. DPM_Solver++ results omitted from the main tables remain in the appendix.

E3.justification: New protocols include point-cloud CD-MMD/CD-COV/JSD evaluation, docking with 40 confidence-ranked candidates and RMSD thresholds, and an NCSN++ backbone-matched consistency-distillation comparison. V3 Appendix D.1.2–D.1.3 also revises phase-two training from five to three epochs and radius scaling from image to latent dimensions. The ImageNet teacher entry changes from 20 to 10 NFE, resolving a v2 inconsistency. These reported corrections do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds point-cloud and docking case studies, including the conformer-alignment example in Figure 9, and replaces several isolated image comparisons with qualitative NFE sweeps using shared initial noise in Figures 18–22. The component ablations, solver-transfer test, radius and data-size analyses, training curves, and prompt-robustness analysis are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Section 5 explicitly mentions three random seeds for the latent ImageNet and LSUN experiments; v3 removes that statement. This changes reporting, without establishing fewer actual runs. The five-run prompt experiment and the uncertainty values in the AYS comparison remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial point-cloud, docking, teacher-reference, and NCSN++ results. For example, Table 10 reports six-NFE docking top-1 success of 35.31% for LD3 versus 32.77% for uniform discretization. Table 22 corrects the first four heuristic rows previously swapped between DPM_Solver++ and iPNDM. The distillation tables add PD results at two and four NFE while omitting the earlier one-NFE CD/RF entries. Most existing image-generation scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: The KL-divergence bound, invertibility and zero-loss assumptions, mathematical objectives, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. The new applications do not introduce additional theoretical results or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: lightweight, solver-adaptable discretization learning without retraining the denoising network. The headline CIFAR10 and AFHQv2 results remain 2.38 and 2.27 FID at ten NFE. New applications provide additional support for existing applicability claims.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly states that LD3 must be trained separately for each NFE. Appendix C develops the training-cost versus inference-speed tradeoff and acknowledges architectural differences in the PD comparison. New application interpretations include an unsupported statement that eight-NFE LD3 surpasses teacher coverage: Table 9 reports 47.12% for both.

D1.justification: V3 documents new application details, including 32 point-cloud training pairs, 10 docking pairs, teacher budgets, and code sources. It adds backbone identities and sources or estimates for distillation training costs, while correcting several existing training instructions. Most optimizer, learning-rate, initialization, and rematerialization details are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for ShapeNet, DiffDock, molecular-docking background, and Consistency Models Made Easy. Appendix C expands positioning relative to the already discussed distillation methods. The main related-work taxonomy and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose is retained with localized editing. The brief main-text distillation discussion becomes a dedicated appendix with three subsections; an appendix contents page is added, existing appendices are relabeled, and publication headers and acknowledgements are updated.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: v2 Figure 5 is replaced by new main-text comparisons, new application figures and tables are added, and appendix image galleries become multi-method NFE grids. The distillation table is split into three tables, Table 7 is restructured, and Tables 2 and 4 are condensed while adding teacher rows. Several existing figures and tables are also relocated.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2's image-only evaluation and aggregate distillation comparison, v3 provides broader empirical support and a more informative backbone-matched comparison with explicit training/inference tradeoffs. Corrected ImageNet row assignments and training instructions also improve reliability. These benefits yield a modest net improvement, tempered by removal of seed information and the incorrect teacher-coverage claim in Appendix B; the central theory and most existing results remain unchanged.
